key_insight: The paper introduces a neural-network wavefunction ansatz plus a hybrid training strategy that can solve the full electron-nuclear Schrödinger equation across diverse molecular systems with a single model.
engineering_relevance: This enables globally accurate potential energy surfaces and full quantum simulations beyond the Born-Oppenheimer approximation, which is valuable for reaction dynamics, excited-state chemistry, and strongly correlated systems.
method: Quantum-chemically inspired orbital-based neural wavefunction with explicit electron-electron correlation
Wavefunction parameters depend on the full electron-nuclear configuration, supporting multi-reference and strongly correlated states
Hybrid optimization combines variational Monte Carlo with local-energy constraints to reduce sampling bias and statistical error
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful evaluation on strongly correlated diatomic molecules, triatomic reactions with conical intersections, and polyatomic multi-reference molecules using a single training framework.
watch_item: Performance likely depends on careful sampling and optimization stability, so scaling to larger systems may still be computationally demanding.
paper_title: Smart Machine Learning for Solving the Full Electron-Nuclear Schrödinger Equation with a Quantum-Chemically Inspired Wavefunction Ansatz
